boundary: Evidence interpretation only. Original method reports, judge decisions and ledger entries remain frozen; no finding feeds back into method execution.

facts: Both reports describe the same authored root initial edge to PoweredOff and a separate PoweredOff-to-Operate transition triggered by start.
Both reports require the root initial edge to target Operate directly. Their titles, citations and wording differ.
Round 1 is INVALID/D0: the judge accepts the structural fact but reads start as the turn-on signal, allowing PoweredOff before power-on.
Round 2 is VALID_NOVEL/D2: the judge reads powering on as an obligation on the root initial edge, rejecting the later start transition as a substitute.
Both method cells were generated on the old provider. The two judge cells use different registered provider profiles and were called at different times.
cases.interpretation: The disputed step is the normative inference from power-on to unconditional root initialization, not the existence of the authored edges. The recorded classifications demonstrate sensitivity to requirement interpretation and report/judge conditions.
cases.causal_limit: Report wording, judge provider and judge time vary together. This comparison does not identify a provider effect or prove that disabling predicates caused a factual hallucination.

facts: The cell emits 10 reports, classified as 1 K, 9 N and 0 I.
Issues 2 and 7 both claim that Interception_Detected has declared consumer transition:line:24 but no reachable consumer. One uses a scope locus, the other an event locus.
Issues 3 and 8 both claim that Task_Assignment_Received has declared consumer transition:line:25 but no reachable consumer, again with scope versus event loci.
The paired reports have different derived contract IDs and neither pair was folded into one published report.

Issue 10 separately reports the unreachable operating scope and includes a folded event-consumer consequence. Its root scope is named UAVSwarmStateMachine, whereas other reports use the natural-language name UAV swarm operation.
cases.interpretation: N counts valid reports outside the ledger, including overlapping claims. Differences in contract identity and locus representation survive the existing publication merge, so these nine N reports cannot be read as nine independent new defects.
cases.causal_limit: The audit establishes concrete report overlap. It does not assign a unique defect count, change K/N/I, or isolate how much of the overlap was caused by the predicate ablation.

facts: Round-1 contract_completion admitted no additional contract or transition group.
Round-1 discovery_grounding branch 0 introduced additional PumpState and WaterState default-entry obligations. Its basis inferred unconditional entry from the required pump and monitoring behavior.
The method published these two claims at internal D2. The external judge retained the authored trigger facts but rejected the unconditional-entry obligation, classifying both as INVALID/D0.
Round 2 published closely corresponding PumpState and WaterState unconditional-entry claims and another for MethaneState.

The round-2 judge likewise classified their core defect class as D0 but assigned FULL relations to INS-0002-03, INS-0002-04 and INS-0002-05. Under the same relation-first closure, all three final report classes are VALID_KNOWN.
The two rounds use the same frozen judge protocol hash and closure settings. The sampled report wording, judge provider, invocation time and relation decisions differ.
cases.interpretation: There are two distinct issues: grounding can infer a stronger normative obligation than the cited NL states, and relation-first ownership can classify a D0 report as K after a positive ledger relation. The strict D2/D1 sensitivity excludes these reports while the main K/N/I accounting retains the frozen labels.
cases.causal_limit: These are traced generation and adjudication facts, not an isolated causal estimate of predicate value or provider quality. No judge result, expected relation or ledger item is rewritten to remove the discrepancy.

facts: The original D request correctly pairs i5 with the initial-transition trigger, i6 with the compound takeover label, and i7 with unresolved Autonomous-mode containment.

The provider's original SemanticDecisionResponse action assigns the takeover-label D2 reasoning to i5 and containment-unresolved reasoning to i6, then omits i7. The error exists in the provider action before runner collection.
validate_d records initial_missing_ids=['0050:r1:i7'], no duplicate or invalid decisions, and a successful correction for i7. The returned i5 and i6 decisions remain frozen by ID.

Consequently the precisely bound takeover-label candidate i6 receives D_UNRESOLVED and is not published; the initial-trigger report i5 is published with takeover reasoning attached. Its externally judged report text still concerns the authored initial trigger.

The source-divergence candidate i6 also carries a front_distance > 10 requirement quote, although its observed clause concerns the separate takeover transition. This source-anchor problem is distinct from response ID misalignment.
v61 publishes the same core compound-label observation as issue:12 and receives D1/K with FULL coverage of EIS-0050-01.
evidence_pointers: llm/method/0050/round-1/d-adjudication/cell-attempt-1/audit.jsonl records context(seq=1), action(seq=10); original stream retained in runs, hash indexed in raw/transport_audit.json
cases.interpretation: Exact ID coverage repair does not establish semantic content alignment. The immediate loss is traceable to the returned D content, not an absent candidate or a failed backend. Generation and review must preserve content-ID correspondence; a lexical similarity validator would not be a sound semantic check.
cases.causal_limit: This case establishes an observed model-response error. It does not prove the error is specific to A2, estimate its corpus-wide prevalence, or authorize quality-based resampling. All original decisions remain frozen.

facts: Anonymous R0004 maps to 0009:r2:issue:7, a twelve-transition guard-carrier aggregate. Its original serialized claim, where, expected, observed and basis contain no FinishState exit transition or dist_to_exit threshold.

The final FULL relation R0004/E0001 says R0004 explicitly enumerates cruise -> FinishState and lane_change -> FinishState with dist_to_exit<2. R0004/E0002 similarly claims lane_change_urban -> FinishState with dist_to_exit<0.7. These purported report contents are absent from the original report.

The relation report_text_evidence repeats complete genuine report fields, but those fields do not contain the asserted exit transitions. Exact quotation and an artifact-compatible validity certificate do not validate the semantic relation rationale.
E0001 and E0002 correctly map to EIS-0009-01 and EIS-0009-02. Their ledger text contains the exit transitions, so this is not an anonymous-ID mapping error in the serialized input.
Both gained expected-round hits also have other FULL support: R0003 supplies E0001 and R0007 supplies E0002. Removing only the erroneous R0004 relations would leave both frozen hit values unchanged.
cases.interpretation: A positive relation rationale can import ledger/artifact facts that the candidate report never states, despite retaining exact full-field quotations. The archived automatic labels and all supporting alternatives must be audited together before interpreting hit changes as discovery gains.
cases.causal_limit: This is a concrete relation-content error, not a prevalence estimate or a corrected human judgment. No original report, relation, hit or metric is altered, and the two hits cannot be discounted solely from this one report.

facts: The original v61 serialized Judge input is receipt-hash verified. Reapplying the current unchanged release adapter to its committed method cell reproduces all four CandidateReport objects exactly.

R0004, mapped to 0054:r3:issue:9, describes four conditions represented as event labels: DoorsClosing-to-InMotion and three transitions within InMotion. No field in the complete serialized report contains EmergencyStopping or obstacle.

The final R0004/E0003 FULL_MATCH reason nevertheless says that R0004 explicitly identifies InMotion-to-EmergencyStopping with [obstacle detected] and no separately supplied trigger. Its basis attributes that statement to the report's observed field.

E0003 maps correctly to VU-0054-01, the missing-trigger defect on the authored InMotion-to-EmergencyStopping edge. This is a mismatch between the relation's account of report content and the actual report, not an anonymous-ID decoding error.
The frozen v61 expected outcome has exactly one FULL supporter for VU-0054-01 in round 3: issue:9. Its recorded hit therefore depends on this disputed relation.
The projected CandidateReport has stable_model_hash sha256:86af589ee63540f18e34c9fc503c31de2b7a59a0ea424f0ee8724d42802e3fde.
evidence_pointers: runs/paper1/judge-v61-full-ea6141607/current-r3/inputs/0054.json#/reports/3; original input remains local, while the report projection is reproducible from the committed method cell
cases.interpretation: Content attribution failures occur in both the new A2 judgments and the frozen historical comparison. The presence of an edge in the common artifact closure does not mean the published report claimed that edge. Mechanical accounting can remain internally consistent while semantic relation content is wrong.
cases.causal_limit: All frozen v61 classifications and metrics remain unchanged. This audit identifies one directly dependent historical hit, but it does not authorize relabeling, prove a corrected class, or estimate the prevalence or net bias of relation errors.
